chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim and Abī Qatādah, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man whose garment falls upon a dead donkey: is salat (prayer) valid for him in it before it is washed? He said: "It is not incumbent upon him to wash it; let him pray in it, and there is no harm."

So the proper way regarding this report is that we understand it to mean that when a year has passed over that and it has become bone, then washing the garment because of it is not obligatory. This clarifies what we have mentioned.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), whose validity is being asked about
key_terms.ثَوْبُهُ: his garment, the clothing under discussion for ritual purity
key_terms.حِمَارٍ مَيِّتٍ: a dead donkey, the source of possible impurity in the ruling
key_terms.سَنَةٌ: a year, marking the period after which the carcass is understood differently
key_terms.عَظْمًا: bone, indicating the state of decomposition relevant to the ruling
key_terms.غَسْلُهُ: washing it, meaning cleansing the garment
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm, indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Does a garment need to be washed if it falls on a dead donkey before praying?
ai.summary: This report addresses a legal ruling concerning ritual purity and salat (prayer) when a garment comes into contact with a dead donkey. The closing statement explains that the report is understood in a case where the carcass has decayed and become bone, in which case washing the garment is not required.
